definition: In mathematical optimization, the ordered subset expectation maximization (OSEM) method is an iterative method that is used in computed tomography.
details: In applications in medical imaging, the OSEM method is used for positron emission tomography (PET), for single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and for X-ray computed tomography (X-ray CT) scans. The OSEM method is related to the expectation–maximization (EM) method of statistics. The OSEM method is also related to methods of filtered back projection.

explainer.lead: Ordered subset expectation maximization is an iterative optimization method used in computed tomography. It matters because it underpins image reconstruction in several medical and X-ray scanning modalities.

tiers.eli5: It rebuilds a picture from scanner readings by repeatedly refining its guess, a bit at a time.
tiers.practitioner: It is applied in medical imaging for PET, SPECT and X-ray CT scans, and is related to the expectation-maximization method of statistics and to filtered back projection. A pitfall is that as an iterative method it repeats refinement rather than producing an image in one pass.
tiers.paperLevel: An iterative method in mathematical optimization used in computed tomography, related to expectation-maximization and to filtered back projection, applied to PET, SPECT and X-ray CT.

explainer.example: A PET scanner's readings are reconstructed into an image by repeatedly updating the estimate through OSEM iterations.
